evals.name: narrow-stacked-fixup
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request. Do not use live Git or forge tools; give the branch, publication, and stopping decisions.
evals.expected_output: The agent isolates the narrow fixup from unrelated work, preserves the existing stack relationship, routes commits and pushes through Versionkeeping, and stops before publication when the stack base or reviewer-request scope is ambiguous.
expectations: The response confirms the exact reviewed pull request, stack base, and requested file scope before creating a fixup branch.
The response preserves unrelated local work and blocks a mixed-ownership path from the fixup commit.
The response uses Versionkeeping for the task-owned checkpoint and push, then the appropriate publisher or Graphite transport for the PR relationship.
The response does not rewrite or publish the stack when the parent identity or requested scope remains ambiguous.

evals.name: latest-publication-receipt-drift
evals.prompt: Using the provided scenario fixture, respond as the agent handling this request. Do not use live Git or forge tools; give the exact publication-audit route and final handoff decision.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the publisher's read-only audit after stack publication, treats sequence 5 as authoritative, and blocks the successful fixup handoff because the latest receipt drifts despite an older matching receipt.
expectations: The response invokes audit_reviewable_pr.py audit with the exact fixup PR identity after Graphite transport and canonical publication.
The response uses only sequence 5 as authoritative and does not substitute matching sequence 4.
The response treats drift as a blocker before reporting a verified review handoff.
The response performs no publication replay, retry, reconciliation, ready mutation, or merge actuation.
